subject: knight
pitch: A fantasy knight in battle-worn plate armour. A great helm with a narrow eye slit and a tall crimson plume, layered shoulder plates etched with gold filigree, a deep-blue surcoat with a silver griffin emblem, a tall kite shield bearing the same griffin, and a broadsword. Dents and scratches tell of many battles, and a torn crimson cape hangs from the shoulders.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module using the SDK to build a standing humanoid knight around 1.9m tall, structuring the rest pose with named joints and using the builder's helper functions for joints, chains, and part geometry.

I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root, chest and neck up the spine to the head, then mirrored legs with hip/knee/ankle joints and arms with shoulder/elbow joints, placing approximate coordinates for each along a Y-up, Z-forward axis.

I'm also adding a cape sweeping from the shoulders rigidly on the chest bone and a plume sprouting from the helm, then working out how parts get attached — using explicit bone bindings with literal position arrays, and capsules spanning joint pairs for limbs like the thighs.

For surfaces, I'm leaning on the paints module (mottle, stripes, gradient, etc.) to weather the steel armor, adding thin gold torus trim for filigree on the shoulder plates, and painting the surcoat deep blue with a silver griffin emblem rendered via an SVG texture mapped onto a UV'd part.

For the kite shield, I'll build it with the extrude helper using outline points, then layer a textured plane slightly offset in front for the griffin emblem with alpha cutout.

Now I'm sketching out the module's imports and structure, planning for a moderately sized file around 350 lines that uses the builder, rng, svg, and paint utility functions together.

I'm defining the color palette with steel, dark, gold, crimson, blue, and silver tones, then setting up the builder and spine chain joints with named roles for the rig.

For the limbs I'm working out that a 3-point polyline needs names covering spans plus one tip joint, so I'm structuring leg chains as hip-knee-ankle with an explicit parent reference back to the hips joint to avoid orphaned parenting.

Setting up arm chains similarly from shoulder through elbow to wrist, mirroring the right side with a negative x offset and positioning the sword-holding wrist slightly forward, then adding neck and head joints anchored to the chest with upward-facing directions, and defining hips as the unparented root joint.

Now I'm building the helmet geometry using a lathed profile revolved around the head joint, with points defining a rounded dome shape tapering to a point at top, plus a small dark box to represent the eye slit across the front.

Next I'm considering how to construct the plume, deciding it should be a thin extruded crest sitting atop the helmet, oriented in the sagittal plane so it reads properly when viewed from the side.

Then I'm planning layered pauldrons using stacked lathe shapes of decreasing radius on each shoulder, attached to the chest bone.

For attachment, each pauldron is positioned at the shoulder joint and bound to the "shoulderL" bone, since that joint marks the start of the arm chain. I'm thinking of adding gold trim details—maybe small torus rings as decorative rims rather than painted filigree—rotated to sit flush against each plate, and flattening the lathe profile into a shallow dome shape for the plates themselves.

For the torso, I'm considering a loft along a catmull-rom path through several body stations, weighing whether to bind it to the chest bone directly or let it use nearest-joint weighting for a more natural drape of the surcoat.

I'll bind the torso loft to both the hips and chest bones together so the skin blends smoothly across that joint boundary. For the surcoat itself, I'm planning a wider loft with flaring stations from chest down to hip to hem near the knees, making sure the hem width is generous enough to fully cover the leg cylinders underneath.

For armor, I'm considering adding a steel breastplate as a separate extruded slab shape positioned just in front of the surcoat's chest area, defining a shield-like outline in a front-facing plane and extruding it with some thickness, attached to the chest bone. I need to double check the loft's width/height values represent half-extents so the breastplate sits properly without z-fighting against the surcoat fabric.

For the legs, I'm planning capsule shapes for thighs and shins running from hip to knee and knee to ankle, plus box-shaped feet positioned with a forward offset for boots, and I'm considering steel greave plates layered over the shin capsules for armor coverage.

For the arms, I'm using capsules for upper arm and forearm with joint chain naming, then designing a sword held in the right hand built from an extruded blade outline with a tapering tip, a box crossguard, and a rod grip, sized to roughly broadsword proportions and attached at the wrist joint.

I'm also designing a kite-shaped shield for the left arm using an extruded outline with a pointed bottom, attaching it to a forearm joint, and adding a griffin emblem via a textured plane using a simple SVG silhouette with silver fill on a blue shield field, plus considering a matching griffin motif on the surcoat's lower skirt area.

For the cape, I'm building it as a membrane stretched between two edge paths — a smooth top edge across the shoulders and a jagged, torn-looking bottom hem edge with zigzag points — colored crimson and rigidly bound to the chest bone, hanging down the back.

For surface texture, I'm defining the steel material using a grain-based procedural color pattern for scratches and weathering rather than a flat color, and sticking with plain hex strings for gold, crimson, and blue accents.

Finally I'm detailing the helmet: a lathed dome profile with a gold torus trim band rotated to lie flat, a nasal guard bar, a narrow eye slit positioned based on the helmet's radius at that height, a neck gorget lathe ring, and I'm now starting on a plume/crest attachment at the top of the helmet.

I'm working out the plume as a thin extruded shape rising from the helmet top, built from a small closed outline in the z-y plane to keep it profile-thin and visible from the side, then considering painting it crimson with a grain texture for a weathered look.

I'm adding gold filigree trim rings and small rivet-like spheres onto the pauldrons, then designing the pauldrons themselves as stacked lathe-profile domes of decreasing radius layered upward from the shoulder joint to create an armored shoulder cap look, followed by sphere-based knee and elbow cops in steel.

Writing boot and gauntlet geometry...

I'm finalizing the cape's membrane configuration with explicit edge paths and crimson coloring bound to the chest bone, then moving into writing out literal joint position arrays for the leg and arm chains, calculating hip, knee, ankle, shoulder, elbow, and wrist coordinates so the proportions read naturally, and placing the sword's grip, crossguard, blade, and pommel directly off the right wrist joint with mirrored negative-x coordinates for the right side versus the left.

I'm reasoning through how the chain-building logic assigns joint names across path spans to make sure "hipL/kneeL/ankleL" and arm equivalents map correctly to parent-child joints, and confirming that the chest and hips joints already exist for the torso loft's bone references.

Now I'm beginning to write the actual module: importing the builder utilities, defining color constants for gold, crimson, blue, silver, leather, and dark tones, and setting up grain and mottle-based paints for steel, cloth, and blade surfaces.

Writing paint and constant definitions...

I'm drafting the griffin SVG silhouette by sketching path shapes for the head, beak, neck, wings, tail, and legs in a simple illustrative style, intended as a white silhouette texture that will read as silver or gold depending on the tint color applied, with transparent areas letting the shield's blue field show through.

Writing SVG paths...

I'm working out the shield's extruded kite outline coordinates and its position relative to the left wrist, plus a gold boss sphere on its face, and now I'm positioning the chest breastplate extrusion relative to the torso's z-depth and station height.

Still writing extrude outlines...

I'm placing the griffin emblem plane on the surcoat's front at roughly the hip-to-chest height, and sketching out the loft stations (position, width, height) that define the torso's cloth silhouette from hem to shoulder, deciding on a smooth Catmull interpolation between them.

I'm settling on bone and color parameters for the torso loft, making sure to always pass an explicit color option since the sweep functions require one, and planning to use joint handles (not string names) when calling capsule functions for limbs so they inherit proper rigging weights.

I'm structuring a symmetric left/right loop using a sign multiplier for mirroring x-coordinates, building leg and arm chains with templated joint names like hipL/hipR, extracting the resulting joint objects, and then adding capsule limbs, sphere joints for knees and elbows, and box-shaped boots and gauntlets at the appropriate positions.

Writing gauntlet and boot code...

I'm now generating the pauldron shoulder armor as a loop of three stacked lathe profiles with decreasing radius, defining each profile's outline points and positioning them progressively higher on the shoulder joint to create a layered domed look.

Writing lathe profile points...

I'm adding gold filigree details—a torus ring and small decorative shapes—onto the pauldron rim for ornamentation, then moving to the helm, modeling it as a lathed dome shape anchored to the head joint with a rounded top.

Writing helm lathe profile...

I'm adding helm details like a dark eye slit box, a steel brow ridge, a gold trim torus band, and a nasal guard, then sketching a crimson horsehair plume as a flat extruded outline rising above the helm's dome.

I'm defining the surcoat as a loft sweep across the hips-to-chest bone span with a tagged name, confirming that string bone references resolve correctly through the joint system, and placing the griffin emblem as a textured plane on the surcoat's front.

I'm reasoning through the plane's UV orientation to confirm the griffin texture won't appear mirrored when viewed from the front, given the camera's default +Z-facing orientation, and concluding the shield's emblem will read correctly as well.

I'm building the cape as a membrane stretched between a smooth top edge near the shoulders and a jagged, torn-looking bottom edge made of zigzagging points, tagged with crimson cloth and anchored to the chest bone with a defined row/column grid density.

I'm constructing the sword by extruding a tapered blade outline anchored at the wrist, adding a gold crossguard box, a leather-wrapped cylindrical grip, and a pommel sphere, calculating y-positions so each piece lines up along the arm.

Writing shield extrude code...

I'm placing the shield geometry on the left wrist only, adding a gold boss sphere and a textured griffin plane to its face, and considering subtle weathering effects like grain and mottling across the steel and shield surfaces to sell the "battle-worn" look.

I'm finalizing the module by wrapping everything in an exported build function that returns the builder's root node, double-checking that all geometry options like thickness arrays, rotation vectors, and bone references are typed correctly, and adding a small neck gorget lathe ring as a last detail before considering the model complete.
